channel.title: Doctrines & Laws: Indian law, explained
channel.description: Free plain-language explainers on Indian law: Supreme Court and High Court rulings, statutes and your rights. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: Seven years in jail after acquittal: what does Article 21 owe you?
item.description: The Supreme Court awarded ₹30 lakh in public-law compensation and asked Parliament to enact a law on wrongful incarceration.

item.title: How do I protect my brand name? Trademark basics in India
item.description: File online with IP India for ₹4,500 a class if you are an individual, startup or small business. What registration protects, and what ™ and ® mean.

item.title: Can an online seller refuse a return or a refund?
item.description: Not if the product is defective, fake, not as described or delivered late. What the e-commerce rules say, and how to complain if a platform won’t budge.

item.title: New labour codes: what changed for employees?
item.description: Four codes replaced 29 labour laws on 21 November 2025. Appointment letters, gratuity after one year for fixed-term staff, and what else to know.

item.title: How is crypto taxed in India? The 30% rule explained
item.description: Gains on crypto and other virtual digital assets are taxed at a flat 30%, with 1% TDS on sales. What changed under the Income-tax Act, 2025.

item.title: How many SIM cards can be in your name? Limits and penalties
item.description: Nine across India, six in J&K, Assam and the North-East. How to check the numbers issued in your name, and block the ones you don’t use.

item.title: Is esports legal in India? What the Online Gaming Act says
item.description: Yes. The Online Gaming Act, 2025 recognises e-sports as competitive sport, separate from banned real-money games. How recognition and registration work.

item.title: Lost money to an online fraud? What to do in the first hour
item.description: Call 1930 or report on cybercrime.gov.in at once, then tell your bank. Speed decides whether the money can be frozen before it moves on.

item.title: Is there such a thing as a “digital arrest”?
item.description: No. Indian law has no procedure for arresting anyone over a video call. How the scam works, and what the Supreme Court has ordered.

item.title: When must a social media platform take down a post?
item.description: Section 79 of the IT Act shields platforms only if they act on lawful orders. Since February 2026 the deadline is three hours, not 36.

item.title: Your personal data was leaked. What must the company tell you?
item.description: Under the DPDP Rules, 2025, a company must tell affected users without delay and report to the Data Protection Board within 72 hours.

item.title: Deepfakes and AI-made content: what the 2026 IT Rules require
item.description: Since 20 February 2026, AI-generated audio, images and video must carry a clear label and embedded provenance data. What platforms and AI tools must do.

item.title: Can AI companies train on your work? The ANI v. OpenAI ruling
item.description: The Delhi High Court refused an interim injunction against ChatGPT, finding training prima facie fair dealing. What it decided and what is still open.

item.title: Who can use a celebrity’s face or voice? Personality rights
item.description: Courts protect a well-known person’s name, image, voice and likeness from commercial misuse, including AI deepfakes, voice clones and chatbots.

item.title: UA 7+, 13+, 16+: film certification and piracy law explained
item.description: The 2023 amendment to the Cinematograph Act added age-based ratings, made certificates permanent and made camcording and piracy specific offences.

item.title: What the National Sports Governance Act, 2025 changes
item.description: A National Sports Board now recognises federations and a Sports Tribunal hears disputes, with appeals to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Is real-money online gaming banned in India?
item.description: Yes. Since 1 May 2026 the Online Gaming Act bans offering, advertising and processing payments for online money games. Players are not punished.

item.title: Hidden charges at checkout? Dark patterns explained
item.description: Indian law bans 13 “dark patterns” on apps and websites, from fake countdown timers to items sneaked into your cart. What they are and how to complain.

item.title: Can I file an FIR at any police station? Zero FIR explained
item.description: Yes. Under Section 173 of the BNSS, police must record a cognizable offence wherever it happened and transfer it. How to file, and what to do if refused.

item.title: One dashboard for all your data permissions?
item.description: How Consent Managers under the DPDP Act, 2023 and Rule 4 of the DPDP Rules, 2025 are meant to work.

item.title: Can a government order rely on case law invented by AI?
item.description: The Bombay High Court quashed a customs order that cited judgments that do not exist.

item.title: When does an autonomous body become “State”?
item.description: The Supreme Court held that the National Book Trust is “State” under Article 12.

item.title: Can the police summon you to “settle” a property dispute?
item.description: Police investigate crime; civil courts decide property disputes.

item.title: “Law and order” or “public order”? The concentric circles test
item.description: Why not every crime justifies preventive detention under Article 22.

item.title: Can a WhatsApp screenshot alone get someone convicted?
item.description: Admissibility is one hurdle; proving who wrote the message is another.

item.title: Road accident? Interim relief without proving fault
item.description: Section 164A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 provides for quick interim compensation.

item.title: Can the State ban a protest just to manage traffic?
item.description: Article 19(1)(b), the public trust doctrine and the proportionality test.
